letters.notes: Hamza, second pass (framed as staged: 'Hamza is so complicated in Arabic, so we're going to give it to you gradually ... we'll leave it until the end of the semester'). Never written bare at the start of a word: 'at the beginning of the word it has to have a seat ... the only seat is alif.' Vowel on the alif-hamza decides the sound: fatHa = a, Damma = u, kasra = i and 'it has to be written under the alif.' Alif-hamza can carry a sukuun, 'but we don't write the sukuun.' 'It's a glottal stop.' 'Hamza is not considered a short vowel, it's considered a consonant - that's why it takes fatHa, Damma, kasra and sukuun.' In the middle/end it can sit on alif (ta'ta'a) or 'on the line' after a long alif (baa'): 'we say this is hamza on the line.' Scope: 'For now, what I need you to do: recognize it and learn how to read it ... Later ... we will learn the whys and the hows.'
